_comment_file: Strings that genuinely belong to no single screen. Keep this namespace small: a string used twice is not automatically common, and a shared string that drifts apart in two places is worse than two strings that were always separate. Everything here is loaded before the first paint, so weight matters.

app._comment_name: The product name. Never translated and never transliterated, in any language, including into a non-Latin script.
app.name: Remoter

action._comment_: Verbs on buttons. Imperative, second person, no trailing punctuation, no exclamation marks.

status._comment_working: The accessible name of a spinner whose caller gave it none — read aloud, never drawn. A spinner that names its stage ('Deriving the key…') passes that instead, and should; this is the last resort so that a screen reader never meets an unnamed progress indicator.

window._comment_: The frameless window's own controls. They are drawn by the page, because nothing outside it draws them: without these three buttons the window cannot be minimised, maximised or closed at all. Every label is both the accessible name and the tooltip, so short wins. The application shell's own title bar carries the same four labels at shell.titleBar.* for the main window; if you are translating both, keep them identical.
window._comment_minimise: Verb, imperative: send the window to the taskbar or dock.
window._comment_maximise: Verb, imperative: fill the screen with the window.
window._comment_restore: Verb, imperative: the opposite of Maximise — return the window to its previous size. Not 'restore a backup'.
window._comment_close: Verb, imperative: close the window and quit the application. Not the noun, and not 'close a dialog'.
window._comment_confirmClose: SECURITY-CRITICAL. The last thing standing between the user and permanent, unrecoverable loss — a recovery key that has been shown once and can never be produced again. {atStake} names what would be lost, already phrased as the object of the verb ('your recovery key'). Do not soften 'cannot be undone' into 'may be lost' or a polite hedge; it is literally true and it is the only warning there is.
window.confirmClose: ¿Cerrar Remoter y perder {atStake}? Esto no se puede deshacer.
window._comment_controlFailed: SECURITY-ADJACENT. A window control that refuses and says nothing is indistinguishable from a broken window, which is how the missing controls were noticed in the first place. {action} is one of the four labels above, interpolated rather than concatenated because languages differ on where the subject of this sentence goes. Do not soften this into 'something went wrong'.
window.controlFailed: El gestor de ventanas rechazó la acción {action}.
window.noWindow: Esta página no se está ejecutando dentro de la ventana de Remoter, así que aquí los controles de ventana no hacen nada.

crash._comment_: The screen shown when a component throws while rendering. It is read by someone who has just watched part of the interface disappear, so it says what is still safe before it says anything else. The error's own message is deliberately NOT on this screen: a render error carries interpolated values and this application renders the surroundings of credentials, so the text goes into a details block the user opens on purpose.
crash.title: Algo en la interfaz dejó de funcionar
crash._comment_lead: SECURITY-CRITICAL. The middle sentence is the whole point: a recovery key is shown once and cannot be produced again, so a user who closes this window to 'start fresh' may lose their only way back into the vault. Keep the instruction not to close the window, and keep it before the offer of help.
crash.lead: El resto de Remoter sigue funcionando y no se ha tocado la bóveda. Si había algo a medias que no se puede repetir —una clave de recuperación que todavía no estaba anotada—, no cierre esta ventana: copie los detalles y pida ayuda primero.
crash._comment_retry: Verb, imperative. Narrower than the ordinary 'Try again': it re-renders the part of the interface that threw, and does not retry whatever operation the user was performing.
crash._comment_details: The label of a collapsed disclosure holding the error and the component stack. A noun phrase, not a verb.
crash._comment_copy: Verb, imperative: put those technical details on the clipboard.
crash._comment_copied: Replaces the Copy details label for as long as the copy has succeeded. Past tense, a statement about what just happened.

shortcut._comment_: The keyboard map: one title per action, plus the sentences that explain a binding a user cannot change or cannot reach where they expect. The settings screen renders these; the status bar renders terminalPrefix. Key names themselves — Ctrl, Alt, Shift, Esc, F4 — are NEVER translated and are not in this file.
shortcut._comment_unrebindableNoSetting: Shared by three actions whose keys work but cannot be customised. 'This build' means this released version, not this window or this vault. Say plainly that the shortcut does work — a user reading it is looking at a control that will not let them type a new key, and the first thing they need to know is that the key still fires.
shortcut.unrebindableNoSetting: El archivo de configuración de esta compilación no tiene una entrada para este atajo, así que no habría dónde guardar el cambio. El atajo sí funciona; es fijo.

paletteOpen._comment_title: Opens one overlay that both searches connections and runs commands. 'and', not 'or': it is a single control with two uses.
paletteOpen.title: Paleta de comandos y búsqueda

vaultLock._comment_title: Verb + object: lock the encrypted store, discarding the keys held in memory. Not 'lock the screen'.
vaultLock.title: Bloquear la bóveda

shortcutsCheatsheet._comment_title: A hypothetical overlay listing every shortcut. This build does not have one; the two sentences below say so.
shortcutsCheatsheet.title: Resumen de atajos
shortcutsCheatsheet.unrebindable: No hay nada que reasignar: esta compilación no tiene resumen de atajos, así que ninguna tecla abre uno.
shortcutsCheatsheet._comment_reachNote: 'the table on this screen' is the shortcuts table in Settings, where this sentence is read.
shortcutsCheatsheet.reachNote: Sin asignar. Esta compilación no tiene un panel de resumen de atajos: la tabla de esta pantalla es la referencia.

connectionNew._comment_title: Creates a new saved connection. 'Connection' is the stored record — a host with its protocol and credentials — not the live session opened from it.
connectionNew.title: Nueva conexión

folderNew._comment_title: Creates a new folder in the connection tree.
folderNew.title: Nueva carpeta

connectionConnect._comment_title: Verb + object: open a session to whatever is selected in the tree or the palette.
connectionConnect.title: Conectar lo seleccionado
connectionConnect._comment_unrebindable: Enter here is the keyboard key, never translated.
connectionConnect.unrebindable: Enter pertenece a lo que tenga el foco —un botón, un campo, una fila de una lista—, así que no se toma como atajo global y no se puede reasignar aquí.
connectionConnect.reachNote: Enter conecta desde la paleta de comandos. En el árbol de conexiones solo selecciona; para conectar, haga doble clic o use el menú contextual de la fila.

nodeEdit._comment_title: Verb + object: open the editor for the selected connection or folder. 'selected' is the same word as in Connect selected.
nodeEdit.title: Editar lo seleccionado

tabClose._comment_title: Verb + object: close the session tab that has focus.
tabClose.title: Cerrar la pestaña

tabJump._comment_title: One action bound to nine keys: the first key selects the first tab, the ninth the ninth. The range is written with an en dash and Western digits because the settings table renders it beside the key caps themselves.
tabJump.title: Ir a la pestaña 1–9

sidebarToggle._comment_title: Verb + object: show or hide the connection tree at the side of the window. One key does both, so the title is 'Toggle', not 'Show' or 'Hide'.
sidebarToggle.title: Mostrar u ocultar la barra lateral

inspectorToggle._comment_title: Verb + object: show or hide the panel listing the effective, inheritance-resolved values of the selected node.
inspectorToggle.title: Mostrar u ocultar el inspector

sessionFullscreen._comment_title: Fills the screen with the open session. An adjective phrase describing the state it produces, not an imperative.
sessionFullscreen.title: Sesión a pantalla completa
sessionFullscreen.reachNote: Necesita una sesión abierta: pone a pantalla completa la ventana que la contiene.

terminalFind._comment_title: Searches the scrollback of the terminal that has focus, not the connection tree.
terminalFind.title: Buscar en la terminal
terminalFind.unrebindable: La vista de sesión asigna este atajo por su cuenta, no a través del mapa de atajos, así que esta pantalla no puede cambiarlo.
terminalFind._comment_reachNote: 'Ctrl+Shift chords' names a class of key combinations; Ctrl and Shift are key names and are not translated.
terminalFind.reachNote: Funciona dentro de una terminal con el foco sin necesidad del prefijo: las combinaciones Ctrl+Shift pertenecen a la ventana de la terminal, no al shell remoto.

terminalPrefix._comment_: A hint at the end of the status bar, visible only while a terminal has the keyboard. It is preceded by the prefix's own key caps — Ctrl, Alt — so this reads as the end of a sentence that begins with them and must stay lower case and unpunctuated.
terminalPrefix._comment_explained: The tooltip on that hint. 'prefix' is the extra modifier held alongside a shortcut while a session owns the keyboard.
terminalPrefix.explained: Una terminal con el foco recibe casi todas las pulsaciones. A los atajos propios de Remoter se llega añadiendo este prefijo mientras una sesión tiene el teclado.

strength._comment_: How a password's strength is described while it is being typed. The core sends one number — an entropy estimate in bits — and the interface turns it into these words (apps/desktop/ui/src/i18n/strength.ts), so that the wording follows the reader's language and the digits follow the locale's numbering system. Nothing here may echo the password itself.
strength._comment_label: The four bands, from the same bit thresholds the core scores with. One word each: they sit beside a five-segment meter, not in a sentence.
strength._comment_consequence: What the bit count means as time, at a billion guesses a second. This is the part that changes behaviour — a bit count on its own changes nobody's. The rate is deliberately pessimistic (the vault's own Argon2id makes the real rate orders of magnitude lower) because a reused password is eventually hashed somewhere far weaker, so keep the rate in the sentence.

consequence.instant: Se adivina al instante a mil millones de intentos por segundo.
consequence.seconds: {count, plural, one {Unos # segundo de intentos a mil millones por segundo.} other {Unos # segundos de intentos a mil millones por segundo.}}
consequence.minutes: {count, plural, one {Unos # minuto de intentos a mil millones por segundo.} other {Unos # minutos de intentos a mil millones por segundo.}}
consequence.hours: {count, plural, one {Unas # hora de intentos a mil millones por segundo.} other {Unas # horas de intentos a mil millones por segundo.}}
consequence.days: {count, plural, one {Unos # día de intentos a mil millones por segundo.} other {Unos # días de intentos a mil millones por segundo.}}
consequence.months: {count, plural, one {Unos # mes de intentos a mil millones por segundo.} other {Unos # meses de intentos a mil millones por segundo.}}
consequence.years: {count, plural, one {Unos # año de intentos a mil millones por segundo.} other {Unos # años de intentos a mil millones por segundo.}}
consequence.centuries: Siglos de intentos a mil millones por segundo.
consequence.universe: Más que la edad del universo a mil millones de intentos por segundo.

punctuation._comment_chainSeparator: Joins the hops of a jump-host chain: bastion → gateway → db-01. A locale whose readers expect a different glyph may change it; the arrow is NOT flipped for right-to-left, because each hop is wrapped in a Unicode isolate and the chain reads in the document's direction.
punctuation._comment_listSeparator: Only for lists the interface builds itself. Prose lists go through Intl.ListFormat, which knows that English says 'a, b and c' and German says 'a, b und c'.
punctuation._comment_factSeparator: Joins short facts on one line that are not a prose list: 'Password only · Argon2id, 256 MiB, t=3 · Added 3 Mar 2025'. A locale whose readers expect a different glyph may change it; the spaces around it are part of the separator. Not flipped for right-to-left — a middot has no direction.
